ElectroTech Ireland Appoints New Managing Director to Drive Expansion

ElectroTech Ireland, a leading supplier in the country’s electrical equipment sector, has announced the appointment of Niamh O’Donnell as its new Managing Director, effective immediately. The move comes as the company seeks to strengthen its position in the Irish market and expand its portfolio of commercial and industrial solutions.

O’Donnell, who brings over 20 years of experience in the European electrical equipment industry, most recently served as Chief Operations Officer at PowerGrid Solutions. In her new role, she will oversee ElectroTech’s strategic development, operational efficiency, and engagement with key partners across the island.

“We are delighted to welcome Niamh to ElectroTech Ireland,” said Seamus Kavanagh, Chair of the Board. “Her proven track record in driving growth and innovation is precisely what we need as we enter our next phase. With the Irish market evolving rapidly, her appointment underscores our commitment to investing in local leadership and expertise.”

According to the Electrical Industries Federation of Ireland (EIFI), the sector contributed €1.4 billion to the Irish economy last year, buoyed by strong demand from data centre construction and the ongoing roll-out of renewable energy projects. “With energy efficiency and sustainability now top priorities, companies like ElectroTech are well-positioned to support Ireland’s transition to a greener grid,” said EIFI spokesperson Fiona Lyons.

O’Donnell highlighted her focus on digitalisation and workforce development. “We are at an exciting juncture, with opportunities to leverage digital tools and upskill our teams for the future,” she said. “I look forward to working with our talented staff and partners to deliver innovative solutions for our customers.”

The appointment has been widely welcomed by industry observers, who note that strengthening leadership at established firms will be key as Ireland’s electrical equipment sector adapts to shifting technology and regulatory landscapes.
